limitations: The amount of calculation confines the prediction to 2D modeling in the validity tests.
Future work needs to enable 3D simulations to be conducted under high-frequency conditions to investigate issues such as the height of the spaces.
Future work should consider rooms with circular and irregular shapes and rooms connected at the corner.
minimum_safe_summary: This empirical study used a 2D finite element model with field validation to parametrically investigate acoustic modeling in sequential spaces. Key findings include that in rooms with high absorption, larger opening dimensions lead to higher average SPL and smaller level differences between rooms, while opening position significantly impacts SPL only for low absorption rooms. Oblique sound radiation results in larger level differences than horizontal radiation. An additional sound source in a room can maintain or reduce SPL in that room by ~10 dB, but increases SPL in other rooms with high absorption. Adjustments to low absorption coefficients have more significant effects on SPL, and nonuniform absorption distribution leads to greater SPL differences for smaller openings. Finally, the effect of adding more sequential rooms on the first receiving room's SPL is less when absorption in those rooms is high, with a maximum difference of ~6 dB depending on the number of rooms. Limitations include the current confinement to 2D modeling and the need for future 3D simulations to investigate height and complex room geometries.
